description: The SIXTH and LAST arm of the custom range's ordered blank chain, reached only by making every one of the five arms above it fall through - which is the assertion. CUSTOMI arrives as 'X' - not 'Y' - so the outer ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :212 falls past the Monthly arm at :213 and the Yearly arm at :239 and matches the third at :256, whose condition is 'CUSTOMI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES': any non-blank byte selects it, and using 'X' is what proves the arm is chosen by non-blankness rather than by the letter 'Y'. Inside it the ordered chain at :258-303 is entered and walked in full: :259 'SDTMMI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES' is tested and FALLS THROUGH because SDTMMI is '07'; :266 SDTDDI falls through on '01'; :273 SDTYYYYI falls through on '2022'; :280 EDTMMI falls through on '07'; :287 EDTDDI falls through on '31'; and only then does :294 'EDTYYYYI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES' MATCH, because EDTYYYYI is four spaces. EXACTLY ONE of the six parts is blank and it is the LAST one, so the outcome is attributable to the sixth arm alone and cannot be explained by any earlier match - the chain's order is genuinely asserted rather than merely assumed (gate G30). This is the MIRROR of case14, which arranges the same chain so that the FIRST arm fires; between them the two files pin the ordering from both ends. The trailing 'WHEN OTHER -> CONTINUE' at :301-302 is NOT reached here, and that arm is the one case16 relies on - its ten items are all non-blank, so the chain falls to its default and execution carries on into the NUMVAL-C store at :313 - so case15 and case16 together cover the whole chain including its default. :296 moves 'End Date - Year can NOT be empty...' into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80), :298 raises WS-ERR-FLG, :299 moves -1 into EDTYYYYL and :300 performs SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE CASE. SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN ends at :580 with GO TO RETURN-TO-CICS - this program's SINGLE GO TO, verified as the only one in the file and classified as a benign shared terminal - and RETURN-TO-CICS at :585-591 issues EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which ends the task. Control NEVER returns to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, so on this path: the six FUNCTION NUMVAL-C stores at :305-327 DO NOT EXECUTE, which is why the ten echoed items below are the RAW received bytes and EDTYYYYO is still four spaces rather than a normalised '0000'; the six validity IFs at :329-379 do not execute, so the operator is never told the year is invalid, only that it is empty; NEITHER CSUTLDTC call site - :392 for the start date, :412 for the end date - is reached, so util.DateUtilityJob is NOT INVOKED AT ALL and a strict double would see zero interactions; the IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON blocks at :434 and :445 are never reached, so there is no DFHGREEN and no submitted-for-printing notice; and no EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD at :517 occurs, so nothing whatsoever reaches the job-submission port. In Java the shared finalisation must be followed by an immediate return from the WHOLE handler rather than by a helper that merely returns to its caller - the latter would let execution fall into the NUMVAL-C block and would break parity silently while still looking correct (rule R7, practice B5: the terminal-GO-TO structure and the unreachability it creates are behaviour to reproduce, not a defect to repair). Gate G32 does not apply; CBSTM03A is the only program with backward loop-forming GO TOs. THE EMPTY PORT STREAM IS ASSERTED, NOT IMPLIED: expectedWrites is empty, which this model defines as a positive assertion that nothing was written, and FieldDiffer enforces it in BOTH directions - had one record been handed over, its EXTRA_DATASET pass would report the JOBS dataset this case pins nothing from (negative gate G42). It is expressed that way rather than as a zero-row expectedDatasets entry because the queue is OPENTIME(INITIAL) and this program issues no OPEN, so 'opened and wrote nothing' is not a state the COBOL can be in and the fingerprint deliberately never reports it. GATE G38, CORRECTED FOR THIS PROGRAM: CORPT00C copies NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY - its verified COPY list at :138-149 is COCOM01Y, CORPT00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - and a search of the whole program for a DFH colour or attribute mnemonic returns exactly one hit, DFHGREEN at :448, on the success path this case never reaches. There is therefore NO DFHRED move and NO '*' marker, and none is fabricated here. The error presentation is asserted as what the program actually does: the byte-exact ERRMSGO text, the -1 cursor on the offending field's own length item, and ERRMSGC left at DFHDFCOL - the default-colour mnemonic - because the red of that field is DECLARATIVE, coming from 'ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET), COLOR=RED, LENGTH=78, POS=(23,1)' in app/bms/CORPT00.bms:218-221 rather than from any MOVE. Note that EDTYYYYL is recorded as cursorField METADATA and never as a payload member: only xxxI and xxxO items are payload, while xxxL, xxxF and xxxA are length, flag and attribute metadata. Contrast case14, whose cursor is SDTMML; SDTMML, MONTHLYL and CONFIRML are NOT the cursor field here. WIDTHS, COUNTED: the literal at :296 is exactly 35 characters with the casing 'can NOT be' preserved verbatim and not normalised; in WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) it is 35 + 45 spaces, and :560 moves it to ERRMSGO PIC X(78), an alphanumeric move that truncates on the right, giving 35 + 43 spaces. Both channels are pinned so that the two-byte truncation stays observable. EDTYYYYI is PIC X(4) at app/cpy-bms/CORPT00.CPY:108, so its blank is four spaces and not one - corroborated by 'EDTYYYY DFHMDF ... LENGTH=4 ... INITIAL=' at app/bms/CORPT00.bms:188-193. TITLE01O is 6 spaces + 'AWS Mainframe Modernization' + 7 spaces = 40, and TITLE02O is 14 spaces + 'CardDemo' + 18 spaces = 40 - taken from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy line 22, because LINE 21 IS COMMENTED OUT and is not the active value. The clock is PINNED at 2022-07-15T10:30:45 (practice B7, no wall-clock and no random value): POPULATE-HEADER-INFO reads it at :611 and :620 takes WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), so CURDATEO is '07/15/22' and CURTIMEO is '10:30:45'. The custom path takes its range from the screen and reads the clock only for the header. The unit kind is CONTROLLER_POJO: ReportRequestController is constructed as a plain Java object and called through mainPara directly - no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no server-side session (gates G51, G37); the commarea, the AID and the screen values all travel in the payload. The AID is named as the DFHAID mnemonic DFHENTER, reproduced by common.CicsAid because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and ABSENT from this repository (risk R-D). The code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII and is never the platform default (practice B8). PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy-bms/CORPT00.CPY, app/bms/CORPT00.bms, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy and app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy - it is NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment (risk R-A, practice B12). Those sources are read-only and were not modified (practice B3), and nothing here is a placeholder (practice B1). NO USER RULES GOVERN THIS FILE: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar - enterprise-standard practices B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8 and B12 are applied in their place. RECORDED OVERLAP, not silently resolved (practice B4): case13 pins this same :294 arm with CUSTOMI 'Y' and a 2026 clock. This case is kept distinct on the two axes the scenario itself supplies - the 'X' selector, which proves :256 tests non-blankness rather than a specific letter, and the 2022 clock, which exercises the :620 two-digit-year substring at a different year - and case13 is left untouched. That is exactly case14's relationship to case12, so the four files form a 2x2 over the two ends of the chain and the two selector-and-clock arrangements.
